reply.text:
Three hours a day is a lot, and I wouldn't build it. Doing that every day with no real rest is a fast route to burnout, nagging overuse problems and poor sleep, and the extra work tends to cost you the strength you're trying to keep. It also isn't the lever people think it is, because weight loss is driven mostly by how you eat over weeks, and training you can repeat beats training you can't.

Whether that volume is safe for your body is a question for your doctor, especially if you're newer to cardio or coming off a break. I can't promise how fast anything will move the scale.

What I'd do instead is a steady base of cardio you can recover from, lifting a few days a week to hold onto muscle, and the app can set your calorie targets for a cut. Want me to set that up?
